title: Boost Linear Algebra Computation Performance via Efficient VNNI Utilization
problem: Existing auto-vectorizers fail to recognize VNNI's unique computation patterns and produce suboptimal code through constrained peephole optimizations, while auto-tuning frameworks require sophisticated pattern templates and extensive search processes.
motivation: VNNI provides significantly higher efficiency for dense linear algebra computations than conventional SIMD instructions, making better utilization critical for performance.
method: The paper improves the pattern recognition in an auto-vectorizer (the compiler tool that converts regular code into fast vector instructions) so it can identify VNNI patterns in linear algebra operations. It does this with more sophisticated matching techniques than traditional approaches, which only look at small code snippets. Because the auto-vectorizer can now spot these patterns, it generates well-optimized code immediately, reducing the need for auto-tuning (the expensive trial-and-error process of testing many code variations to find the fastest one).
key_novelty: The key idea is teaching auto-vectorizers to spot VNNI computation patterns directly, so they generate fast code without needing expensive auto-tuning.
contributions: Improved pattern matching for detecting VNNI-suitable linear algebra computations
More effective code generation for VNNI utilization
Practical compiler-based optimization with reduced overhead
Better performance than existing auto-vectorizers and auto-tuning frameworks
